# OXIDE v2 developer entrypoint (ADR-0011: one Python package). `mise run verify`
# is the one check, and CI (.github/workflows/ci.yml) runs exactly it; before a push,
# `mise run pythons` also runs platforms.yml's other Python versions. uv manages
# Python (.python-version) and dependencies (pyproject.toml, uv.lock).
min_version = "2024.1.0"

[tools]
uv = "0.12.22"

[tasks.bootstrap]
description = "Install the locked environment, fetch the pinned FTS extension and the ContextBench corpora"
run = [
  "uv sync --locked",
  "uv run --locked oxide prepare",
  # Pinned commits for the context-quality gate (fixtures/eval/README.md); cached.
  "uv run --locked python tests/python/contextbench.py fetch",
]

[tasks.lint]
description = "Ruff lint and format check of the engine and its tests"
run = [
  "uv run --locked ruff check src tests/python",
  "uv run --locked ruff format --check src tests/python",
]

[tasks.typecheck]
description = "mypy --strict over src/ and tests/python/"
run = "uv run --locked mypy"

[tasks.test]
description = "pytest: every test and subprocess uses a private data location"
run = "uv run --locked pytest"

[tasks.contextbench-ts]
description = "TypeScript context-quality gate (fixtures/eval/contextbench-ts): ~1.2 GB of pinned corpora, not part of verify"
run = [
  "uv run --locked python tests/python/contextbench_ts.py fetch",
  "OXIDE_CONTEXTBENCH_TS=1 uv run --locked pytest tests/python/test_contextbench_ts.py",
]

[tasks.pythons]
description = "The CI Python matrix locally (platforms.yml py3.12/py3.14 rows): mypy and pytest, xdist like CI"
run = '''
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
# verify runs only .python-version; CI also runs the ends of requires-python, in
# xdist workers. Same commands and flags, newest patch release like CI's runners, and
# an unlimited stack like theirs: 3.14 bounds recursion by the C stack, not a count.
ulimit -s unlimited 2>/dev/null || ulimit -s "$(ulimit -H -s)"
for py in 3.12 3.14; do
  uv python install -q --upgrade "$py"
  export UV_PYTHON="$py" UV_PROJECT_ENVIRONMENT="${XDG_CACHE_HOME:-$HOME/.cache}/oxide/venv-py$py"
  uv run --locked mypy
  uv run --locked pytest -q -n "${OXIDE_JOBS:-2}" --dist loadfile \
    --ignore=tests/python/test_contextbench.py --ignore=tests/python/test_contextbench_ts.py
done
'''

[tasks.verify]
description = "Everything CI checks, in order: lint, typecheck, test"
run = '''
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
# Sequential on purpose: stop at the first failure.
mise run lint
mise run typecheck
mise run test
'''

name: CI

# OXIDE v2: runs exactly `mise run verify` — the same command used locally
# (Ruff, mypy --strict, pytest over the Python engine; ADR-0011).
on:
  pull_request:
    branches: [main, rewrite/v2]
  push:
    branches: [main]

# One run per change: PR runs cancel when superseded; main pushes (run_id) never do.
concurrency:
  group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.head_ref || github.run_id }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  verify:
    name: Verify
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
      - name: Install pinned uv
        uses: jdx/mise-action@v5
        with:
          version: 2026.9.14
          install_args: uv
      - name: Restore the ContextBench corpora cache
        uses: actions/cache@v6
        with:
          path: ~/.cache/oxide
          key: oxide-cache-linux-x86_64-${{ hashFiles('src/oxide/storage/ladybug.py', 'fixtures/eval/contextbench-py/tasks.json') }}
      # The corpora stay cached; the FTS build is always fetched cold, so a replaced
      # upstream build cannot hide behind the cache (docs/fts-mirror/RELEASE.md).
      - name: Drop the cached FTS extension
        run: rm -f ~/.cache/oxide/ladybug-extensions-*/libfts.lbug_extension
      - name: Install locked environment, verify the FTS extension, fetch the corpora
        run: mise run bootstrap
      - name: mise run verify
        run: mise run verify
        env:
          MISE_AUTO_INSTALL: "false"
          # Parallel in CI only; loadfile keeps a file's shared corpora fixture in one worker.
          PYTEST_ADDOPTS: -n auto --dist loadfile
name: Platforms

# Cross-platform verification of the Python engine (docs/platforms.md): on every
# supported platform, the locked environment installs, `oxide prepare` fetches that
# platform's pinned FTS build, mypy and the test suite run from the checkout, and the
# built wheel and sdist pass scripts/smoke_dist.py from a fresh environment.
# ContextBench quality gates stay in ci.yml (Linux) and `mise run contextbench-ts`.
on:
  pull_request:
    branches: [main, rewrite/v2]
  push:
    branches: [main]
  workflow_dispatch:

# One run per change: PR runs cancel when superseded; main pushes (run_id) never do.
concurrency:
  group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.head_ref || github.run_id }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  platform:
    name: ${{ matrix.label }}
    # Intel macOS is the slowest runner (retired by GitHub in 2027): it runs on main
    # pushes and manual runs, not on PRs. The label picks the runner, so exclude works.
    runs-on: >-
      ${{ fromJSON('{"windows-x86_64": "windows-2025", "macos-x86_64": "macos-15-intel",
      "macos-arm64": "macos-15"}')[matrix.label] || 'ubuntu-24.04' }}
    timeout-minutes: 60
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        # ladybug 0.21.0's macOS wheels need macOS 15 or later.
        label: [linux-x86_64, windows-x86_64, macos-x86_64, macos-arm64,
                linux-x86_64-py3.12, linux-x86_64-py3.14]
        # The ends of requires-python; the other rows use .python-version (3.13).
        include:
          - { label: linux-x86_64-py3.12, python: "3.12" }
          - { label: linux-x86_64-py3.14, python: "3.14" }
        exclude:
          - label: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' && 'macos-x86_64' || 'none' }}
    env:
      UV_PYTHON: ${{ matrix.python }}  # empty: .python-version
    defaults:
      run:
        shell: bash
    steps:
      # Fixtures and frozen spans are byte-exact: no CRLF conversion on Windows.
      - run: git config --global core.autocrlf false
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
      - name: Install pinned uv
        uses: jdx/mise-action@v5
        with:
          version: 2026.9.14
          install_args: uv
      # Windows prerequisite (docs/platforms.md): ladybug's wheel excludes OpenSSL 3.
      - name: OpenSSL 3 DLLs in the system directory
        if: runner.os == 'Windows'
        run: |
          dll=$(ls /c/Program\ Files/OpenSSL*/bin/libssl-3-x64.dll 2>/dev/null | head -n 1 || true)
          if [ -z "$dll" ]; then
            choco install -y --no-progress openssl
            dll=$(ls /c/Program\ Files/OpenSSL*/bin/libssl-3-x64.dll | head -n 1)
          fi
          cp "$dll" "$(dirname "$dll")/libcrypto-3-x64.dll" /c/Windows/System32/
      # Not cached: every run fetches the pinned FTS build cold, so a replaced or missing
      # upstream build fails here instead of hiding behind a cache (docs/fts-mirror/RELEASE.md).
      - name: Install the locked environment and the FTS extension
        run: |
          uv sync --locked
          uv run --locked oxide prepare
          uv run --locked python scripts/smoke_dist.py --environment | tee environment.json
      - name: mypy --strict (this platform's branches)
        run: uv run --locked mypy
      - name: pytest (without the ContextBench corpora gate)
        run: >
          uv run --locked pytest --ignore=tests/python/test_contextbench.py
          --ignore=tests/python/test_contextbench_ts.py
          --junitxml=pytest.xml
        env:
          PYTEST_ADDOPTS: -n auto --dist loadfile
      - name: Build the wheel and sdist
        run: uv build --out-dir dist
      # A lock can hide what a user's pip picks from the wheel's own metadata:
      # by default pip takes the newest release even when it has only an sdist.
      - name: Install the wheel with pip from its own metadata
        run: |
          venv="$RUNNER_TEMP/pip-wheel"
          uv venv -q --seed "$venv"
          python="$venv/bin/python"; [ -x "$python" ] || python="$venv/Scripts/python.exe"
          wheel=$(ls dist/*.whl)
          "$python" -m pip install -q --dry-run --ignore-installed --report "$RUNNER_TEMP/pip.json" "$wheel"
          "$python" -I -c "
          import json, sys
          report = json.load(open(sys.argv[1], encoding='utf-8'))['install']
          built = [f\"{i['metadata']['name']} {i['metadata']['version']}\" for i in report
                   if not i['download_info']['url'].endswith('.whl')]
          sys.exit(f'pip would build from source: {built}' if built else 0)" "$RUNNER_TEMP/pip.json"
          "$python" -m pip install -q --only-binary :all: "$wheel"
          "$python" -m pip check
          (cd "$RUNNER_TEMP" && "$python" -I "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/scripts/smoke_dist.py" "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/fixtures")
      - name: Smoke-test each artifact in a fresh environment
        run: |
          uv export --locked --no-dev --no-emit-project --no-hashes -q -o "$RUNNER_TEMP/requirements.txt"
          for artifact in dist/*.whl dist/*.tar.gz; do
            venv="$RUNNER_TEMP/smoke-$(basename "$artifact")"
            uv venv -q "$venv"
            # Third-party dependencies must ship wheels; only OXIDE's sdist is built.
            uv pip install -q --python "$venv" --only-binary :all: -r "$RUNNER_TEMP/requirements.txt"
            uv pip install -q --python "$venv" --no-deps "$artifact"
            uv pip check --python "$venv"
            python="$venv/bin/python"; [ -x "$python" ] || python="$venv/Scripts/python.exe"
            echo "== $artifact"
            (cd "$RUNNER_TEMP" && "$python" -I "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/scripts/smoke_dist.py" "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/fixtures")
          done
      - name: Keep the platform record
        # act (local runs) cannot copy this action into podman containers.
        if: always() && !env.ACT
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v5
        with:
          name: platform-${{ matrix.label }}
          path: |
            environment.json
            pytest.xml
            dist/
          if-no-files-found: ignore

# Cross-platform verification of the Python engine (docs/platforms.md): on every
# supported platform, the locked environment installs, `oxide prepare` fetches that
# platform's pinned FTS build, mypy and the test suite run from the checkout, and the
# built wheel and sdist pass scripts/smoke_dist.py from a fresh environment.
# ContextBench quality gates stay in ci.yml (Linux) and `mise run contextbench-ts`.
on:
  pull_request:
    branches: [main, rewrite/v2]
  push:
    branches: [main]
  workflow_dispatch:

# One run per change: PR runs cancel when superseded; main pushes (run_id) never do.
concurrency:
  group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.head_ref || github.run_id }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  platform:
    name: ${{ matrix.label }}
    # Intel macOS is the slowest runner (retired by GitHub in 2027): it runs on main
    # pushes and manual runs, not on PRs. The label picks the runner, so exclude works.
    runs-on: >-
      ${{ fromJSON('{"windows-x86_64": "windows-2025", "macos-x86_64": "macos-15-intel",
      "macos-arm64": "macos-15"}')[matrix.label] || 'ubuntu-24.04' }}
    timeout-minutes: 60
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        # ladybug 0.21.0's macOS wheels need macOS 15 or later.
        label: [linux-x86_64, windows-x86_64, macos-x86_64, macos-arm64,
                linux-x86_64-py3.12, linux-x86_64-py3.14]
        # The ends of requires-python; the other rows use .python-version (3.13).
        include:
          - { label: linux-x86_64-py3.12, python: "3.12" }
          - { label: linux-x86_64-py3.14, python: "3.14" }
        exclude:
          - label: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' && 'macos-x86_64' || 'none' }}
    env:
      UV_PYTHON: ${{ matrix.python }}  # empty: .python-version
    defaults:
      run:
        shell: bash
    steps:
      # Fixtures and frozen spans are byte-exact: no CRLF conversion on Windows.
      - run: git config --global core.autocrlf false
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
      - name: Install pinned uv
        uses: jdx/mise-action@v5
        with:
          version: 2026.9.14
          install_args: uv
      # Windows prerequisite (docs/platforms.md): ladybug's wheel excludes OpenSSL 3.
      - name: OpenSSL 3 DLLs in the system directory
        if: runner.os == 'Windows'
        run: |
          dll=$(ls /c/Program\ Files/OpenSSL*/bin/libssl-3-x64.dll 2>/dev/null | head -n 1 || true)
          if [ -z "$dll" ]; then
            choco install -y --no-progress openssl
            dll=$(ls /c/Program\ Files/OpenSSL*/bin/libssl-3-x64.dll | head -n 1)
          fi
          cp "$dll" "$(dirname "$dll")/libcrypto-3-x64.dll" /c/Windows/System32/
      # Not cached: every run fetches the pinned FTS build cold, so a replaced or missing
      # upstream build fails here instead of hiding behind a cache (docs/fts-mirror/RELEASE.md).
      - name: Install the locked environment and the FTS extension
        run: |
          uv sync --locked
          uv run --locked oxide prepare
          uv run --locked python scripts/smoke_dist.py --environment | tee environment.json
      - name: mypy --strict (this platform's branches)
        run: uv run --locked mypy
      - name: pytest (without the ContextBench corpora gate)
        run: >
          uv run --locked pytest --ignore=tests/python/test_contextbench.py
          --ignore=tests/python/test_contextbench_ts.py
          --junitxml=pytest.xml
        env:
          PYTEST_ADDOPTS: -n auto --dist loadfile
      - name: Build the wheel and sdist
        run: uv build --out-dir dist
      # A lock can hide what a user's pip picks from the wheel's own metadata:
      # by default pip takes the newest release even when it has only an sdist.
      - name: Install the wheel with pip from its own metadata
        run: |
          venv="$RUNNER_TEMP/pip-wheel"
          uv venv -q --seed "$venv"
          python="$venv/bin/python"; [ -x "$python" ] || python="$venv/Scripts/python.exe"
          wheel=$(ls dist/*.whl)
          "$python" -m pip install -q --dry-run --ignore-installed --report "$RUNNER_TEMP/pip.json" "$wheel"
          "$python" -I -c "
          import json, sys
          report = json.load(open(sys.argv[1], encoding='utf-8'))['install']
          built = [f\"{i['metadata']['name']} {i['metadata']['version']}\" for i in report
                   if not i['download_info']['url'].endswith('.whl')]
          sys.exit(f'pip would build from source: {built}' if built else 0)" "$RUNNER_TEMP/pip.json"
          "$python" -m pip install -q --only-binary :all: "$wheel"
          "$python" -m pip check
          (cd "$RUNNER_TEMP" && "$python" -I "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/scripts/smoke_dist.py" "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/fixtures")
      - name: Smoke-test each artifact in a fresh environment
        run: |
          uv export --locked --no-dev --no-emit-project --no-hashes -q -o "$RUNNER_TEMP/requirements.txt"
          for artifact in dist/*.whl dist/*.tar.gz; do
            venv="$RUNNER_TEMP/smoke-$(basename "$artifact")"
            uv venv -q "$venv"
            # Third-party dependencies must ship wheels; only OXIDE's sdist is built.
            uv pip install -q --python "$venv" --only-binary :all: -r "$RUNNER_TEMP/requirements.txt"
            uv pip install -q --python "$venv" --no-deps "$artifact"
            uv pip check --python "$venv"
            python="$venv/bin/python"; [ -x "$python" ] || python="$venv/Scripts/python.exe"
            echo "== $artifact"
            (cd "$RUNNER_TEMP" && "$python" -I "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/scripts/smoke_dist.py" "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/fixtures")
          done
      - name: Keep the platform record
        # act (local runs) cannot copy this action into podman containers.
        if: always() && !env.ACT
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v5
        with:
          name: platform-${{ matrix.label }}
          path: |
            environment.json
            pytest.xml
            dist/
          if-no-files-found: ignore
name: Claude Code Review

on:
  pull_request:
    types: [opened, synchronize, ready_for_review, reopened]

jobs:
  claude-review:
    # Optional: Filter by PR author
    # if: |
    #   github.event.pull_request.user.login == 'external-contributor' ||
    #   github.event.pull_request.user.login == 'new-developer' ||
    #   github.event.pull_request.author_association == 'FIRST_TIME_CONTRIBUTOR'

    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: read
      pull-requests: read
      issues: read
      id-token: write

    steps:
      - name: Checkout repository
        uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          fetch-depth: 1

      - name: Run Claude Code Review
        id: claude-review
        uses: anthropics/claude-code-action@v1
        with:
          claude_code_oauth_token: ${{ secrets.CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN }}
          plugin_marketplaces: 'https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code.git'
          plugins: 'code-review@claude-code-plugins'
          prompt: '/code-review:code-review --comment ${{ github.repository }}/pull/${{ github.event.pull_request.number }}'
          claude_args: '--allowedTools "mcp__github_inline_comment__create_inline_comment"'
          # See https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code-action/blob/main/docs/usage.md
          # or https://code.claude.com/docs/en/cli-reference for available options

import xml.etree.ElementTree as ET, collections, os
res={}
for l in ['windows-x86_64','linux-x86_64','macos-x86_64','macos-arm64']:
    f=f'{l}/pytest.xml'
    if not os.path.exists(f): continue
    d=collections.Counter(); n=0
    for tc in ET.parse(f).iter('testcase'):
        c=tc.get('classname','')
        d[c]+=float(tc.get('time',0)); n+=1
    res[l]=d; print(l,'tests',n,'sum',round(sum(d.values())))
w=res['windows-x86_64']; L=res['linux-x86_64']
for k,v in w.most_common(25): print(f'{v:7.1f} {L.get(k,0):7.1f} {res.get("macos-x86_64",{}).get(k,0):7.1f} {k}')
EOF

This makes the actual Defender state observable in the logs.

## Before

```
✓ Disable CPU hogs (Windows)   # green even if nothing was disabled
```

## After

```
== Windows Defender status (post disable attempt) ==
RealTimeProtectionEnabled : False
IsTamperProtected         : False
AntivirusEnabled          : True
```

Motivation: a recent `main` Windows build failed at `cargo codegen` with `serde_derive.dll: LoadLibraryExW failed: Invalid access to memory location. (os error 998)`. That loader flake is often attributed to AV scanning freshly-linked proc-macro DLLs, but we currently cannot confirm whether Defender is truly off on these runners. This unblocks that diagnosis without changing the disable behavior itself.

          chore(ci): surface Windows Defender status after disable attempt

```

check does not prove realtime monitoring was actually turned off (Tamper
Protection commonly blocks Set-MpPreference). Print Get-MpComputerStatus
so logs show the real state.
```

web.title: Troubleshooting mode scenarios in Microsoft Defender for Endpoint
web.description:
# Troubleshooting mode scenarios in Microsoft Defender for Endpoint
## Scenario 1: Unable to install application
4. Go to **Windows security** > **Threat & virus protection** > **Manage settings** > **Tamper protection** > **Off**. Alternately, during troubleshooting mode, you can use the PowerShell command `Set-MPPreference -DisableTamperProtection $true` on Windows devices. To check the state of tamper protection, you can use the Get-MpComputerStatus PowerShell cmdlet. In the list of results, look for `IsTamperProtected` or `RealTimeProtectionEnabled`. (A value of _true_ means tamper protection is enabled.)
5. Launch an elevated PowerShell command prompt, and toggle off real-time protection.
   - Run `Set-MpPreference -DisableRealtimeMonitoring $true` to turn off real-time protection.

## Scenario 3: Application taking longer to perform an action
2. To disable real-time protection for this scenario, first turn off tamper protection. You can use the PowerShell command `Set-MPPreference -DisableTamperProtection $true` on Windows devices. To check the state of tamper protection, you can use the Get-MpComputerStatus PowerShell cmdlet. In the list of results, look for `IsTamperProtected` or `RealTimeProtectionEnabled`. (A value of _true_ means tamper protection is enabled.) For more information, see Protect security settings with tamper protection.
4. Launch an elevated PowerShell command prompt, and run the following command: `Set-mppreference -DisableRealtimeMonitoring $true`
5. After disabling real-time protection, check to see if the application is slow.

## See also
- Set-MpPreference

name: Platforms

# Cross-platform verification of the Python engine (docs/platforms.md): on every
# supported platform, the locked environment installs, `oxide prepare` fetches that
# platform's pinned FTS build, mypy and the test suite run from the checkout, and the
# built wheel and sdist pass scripts/smoke_dist.py from a fresh environment.
# ContextBench quality gates stay in ci.yml (Linux) and `mise run contextbench-ts`.
on:
  pull_request:
    branches: [main, rewrite/v2]
  push:
    branches: [main]
  workflow_dispatch:

# One run per change: PR runs cancel when superseded; main pushes (run_id) never do.
concurrency:
  group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.head_ref || github.run_id }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  platform:
    name: ${{ matrix.label }}
    # Intel macOS is the slowest runner (retired by GitHub in 2027): it runs on main
    # pushes and manual runs, not on PRs. The label picks the runner, so exclude works.
    runs-on: >-
      ${{ fromJSON('{"windows-x86_64": "windows-2025", "macos-x86_64": "macos-15-intel",
      "macos-arm64": "macos-15"}')[matrix.label] || 'ubuntu-24.04' }}
    timeout-minutes: 60
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        # ladybug 0.21.0's macOS wheels need macOS 15 or later.
        label: [linux-x86_64, windows-x86_64, macos-x86_64, macos-arm64,
                linux-x86_64-py3.12, linux-x86_64-py3.14]
        # The ends of requires-python; the other rows use .python-version (3.13).
        include:
          - { label: linux-x86_64-py3.12, python: "3.12" }
          - { label: linux-x86_64-py3.14, python: "3.14" }
        exclude:
          - label: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' && 'macos-x86_64' || 'none' }}
    env:
      UV_PYTHON: ${{ matrix.python }}  # empty: .python-version
    defaults:
      run:
        shell: bash
    steps:
      # Fixtures and frozen spans are byte-exact: no CRLF conversion on Windows.
      - run: git config --global core.autocrlf false
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
      - name: Install pinned uv
        uses: jdx/mise-action@v5
        with:
          version: 2026.9.14
          install_args: uv
      # Windows prerequisite (docs/platforms.md): ladybug's wheel excludes OpenSSL 3.
      - name: OpenSSL 3 DLLs in the system directory
        if: runner.os == 'Windows'
        run: |
          dll=$(ls /c/Program\ Files/OpenSSL*/bin/libssl-3-x64.dll 2>/dev/null | head -n 1 || true)
          if [ -z "$dll" ]; then
            choco install -y --no-progress openssl
            dll=$(ls /c/Program\ Files/OpenSSL*/bin/libssl-3-x64.dll | head -n 1)
          fi
          cp "$dll" "$(dirname "$dll")/libcrypto-3-x64.dll" /c/Windows/System32/
      # Not cached: every run fetches the pinned FTS build cold, so a replaced or missing
      # upstream build fails here instead of hiding behind a cache (docs/fts-mirror/RELEASE.md).
      - name: Install the locked environment and the FTS extension
        run: |
          uv sync --locked
          uv run --locked oxide prepare
          uv run --locked python scripts/smoke_dist.py --environment | tee environment.json
      - name: mypy --strict (this platform's branches)
        run: uv run --locked mypy
      - name: pytest (without the ContextBench corpora gate)
        run: >
          uv run --locked pytest --ignore=tests/python/test_contextbench.py
          --ignore=tests/python/test_contextbench_ts.py
          --junitxml=pytest.xml
        env:
          PYTEST_ADDOPTS: -n auto --dist loadfile
      - name: Build the wheel and sdist
        run: uv build --out-dir dist
      # A lock can hide what a user's pip picks from the wheel's own metadata:
      # by default pip takes the newest release even when it has only an sdist.
      - name: Install the wheel with pip from its own metadata
        run: |
          venv="$RUNNER_TEMP/pip-wheel"
          uv venv -q --seed "$venv"
          python="$venv/bin/python"; [ -x "$python" ] || python="$venv/Scripts/python.exe"
          wheel=$(ls dist/*.whl)
          "$python" -m pip install -q --dry-run --ignore-installed --report "$RUNNER_TEMP/pip.json" "$wheel"
          "$python" -I -c "
          import json, sys
          report = json.load(open(sys.argv[1], encoding='utf-8'))['install']
          built = [f\"{i['metadata']['name']} {i['metadata']['version']}\" for i in report
                   if not i['download_info']['url'].endswith('.whl')]
          sys.exit(f'pip would build from source: {built}' if built else 0)" "$RUNNER_TEMP/pip.json"
          "$python" -m pip install -q --only-binary :all: "$wheel"
          "$python" -m pip check
          (cd "$RUNNER_TEMP" && "$python" -I "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/scripts/smoke_dist.py" "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/fixtures")
      - name: Smoke-test each artifact in a fresh environment
        run: |
          uv export --locked --no-dev --no-emit-project --no-hashes -q -o "$RUNNER_TEMP/requirements.txt"
          for artifact in dist/*.whl dist/*.tar.gz; do
            venv="$RUNNER_TEMP/smoke-$(basename "$artifact")"
            uv venv -q "$venv"
            # Third-party dependencies must ship wheels; only OXIDE's sdist is built.
            uv pip install -q --python "$venv" --only-binary :all: -r "$RUNNER_TEMP/requirements.txt"
            uv pip install -q --python "$venv" --no-deps "$artifact"
            uv pip check --python "$venv"
            python="$venv/bin/python"; [ -x "$python" ] || python="$venv/Scripts/python.exe"
            echo "== $artifact"
            (cd "$RUNNER_TEMP" && "$python" -I "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/scripts/smoke_dist.py" "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/fixtures")
          done
      - name: Keep the platform record
        # act (local runs) cannot copy this action into podman containers.
        if: always() && !env.ACT
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v5
        with:
          name: platform-${{ matrix.label }}
          path: |
            environment.json
            pytest.xml
            dist/
          if-no-files-found: ignore
name: CI

# OXIDE v2: runs exactly `mise run verify` — the same command used locally
# (Ruff, mypy --strict, pytest over the Python engine; ADR-0011).
on:
  pull_request:
    branches: [main, rewrite/v2]
  push:
    branches: [main]

# One run per change: PR runs cancel when superseded; main pushes (run_id) never do.
concurrency:
  group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.head_ref || github.run_id }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  verify:
    name: Verify
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
      - name: Install pinned uv
        uses: jdx/mise-action@v5
        with:
          version: 2026.9.14
          install_args: uv
      - name: Restore the ContextBench corpora cache
        uses: actions/cache@v6
        with:
          path: ~/.cache/oxide
          key: oxide-cache-linux-x86_64-${{ hashFiles('src/oxide/storage/ladybug.py', 'fixtures/eval/contextbench-py/tasks.json') }}
      # The corpora stay cached; the FTS build is always fetched cold, so a replaced
      # upstream build cannot hide behind the cache (docs/fts-mirror/RELEASE.md).
      - name: Drop the cached FTS extension
        run: rm -f ~/.cache/oxide/ladybug-extensions-*/libfts.lbug_extension
      - name: Install locked environment, verify the FTS extension, fetch the corpora
        run: mise run bootstrap
      - name: mise run verify
        run: mise run verify
        env:
          MISE_AUTO_INSTALL: "false"
          # Parallel in CI only; loadfile keeps a file's shared corpora fixture in one worker.
          PYTEST_ADDOPTS: -n auto --dist loadfile
name: Claude Code Review

on:
  pull_request:

name: Platforms

# Cross-platform verification of the Python engine (docs/platforms.md): on every
# supported platform, the locked environment installs, `oxide prepare` fetches that
# platform's pinned FTS build, mypy and the test suite run from the checkout, and the
# built wheel and sdist pass scripts/smoke_dist.py from a fresh environment.
# ContextBench quality gates stay in ci.yml (Linux) and `mise run contextbench-ts`.
on:
  pull_request:
    branches: [main, rewrite/v2]
  push:
    branches: [main]
  workflow_dispatch:

# One run per change: PR runs cancel when superseded; main pushes (run_id) never do.
concurrency:
  group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.head_ref || github.run_id }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  platform:
    name: ${{ matrix.label }}
    # Intel macOS is the slowest runner (retired by GitHub in 2027): it runs on main
    # pushes and manual runs, not on PRs. The label picks the runner, so exclude works.
    runs-on: >-
      ${{ fromJSON('{"windows-x86_64": "windows-2025", "macos-x86_64": "macos-15-intel",
      "macos-arm64": "macos-15"}')[matrix.label] || 'ubuntu-24.04' }}
    timeout-minutes: 60
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        # ladybug 0.21.0's macOS wheels need macOS 15 or later.
        label: [linux-x86_64, windows-x86_64, macos-x86_64, macos-arm64,
                linux-x86_64-py3.12, linux-x86_64-py3.14]
        # The ends of requires-python; the other rows use .python-version (3.13).
        include:
          - { label: linux-x86_64-py3.12, python: "3.12" }
          - { label: linux-x86_64-py3.14, python: "3.14" }
        exclude:
          - label: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' && 'macos-x86_64' || 'none' }}
    env:
      UV_PYTHON: ${{ matrix.python }}  # empty: .python-version
    defaults:
      run:
        shell: bash
    steps:
      # Fixtures and frozen spans are byte-exact: no CRLF conversion on Windows.
      - run: git config --global core.autocrlf false
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
      - name: Install pinned uv
        uses: jdx/mise-action@v5
        with:
          version: 2026.9.14
          install_args: uv
      # Windows prerequisite (docs/platforms.md): ladybug's wheel excludes OpenSSL 3.
      - name: OpenSSL 3 DLLs in the system directory
        if: runner.os == 'Windows'
        run: |
          dll=$(ls /c/Program\ Files/OpenSSL*/bin/libssl-3-x64.dll 2>/dev/null | head -n 1 || true)
          if [ -z "$dll" ]; then
            choco install -y --no-progress openssl
            dll=$(ls /c/Program\ Files/OpenSSL*/bin/libssl-3-x64.dll | head -n 1)
          fi
          cp "$dll" "$(dirname "$dll")/libcrypto-3-x64.dll" /c/Windows/System32/
      # Not cached: every run fetches the pinned FTS build cold, so a replaced or missing
      # upstream build fails here instead of hiding behind a cache (docs/fts-mirror/RELEASE.md).
      - name: Install the locked environment and the FTS extension
        run: |
          uv sync --locked
          uv run --locked oxide prepare
          uv run --locked python scripts/smoke_dist.py --environment | tee environment.json
      - name: mypy --strict (this platform's branches)
        run: uv run --locked mypy
      - name: pytest (without the ContextBench corpora gate)
        run: >
          uv run --locked pytest --ignore=tests/python/test_contextbench.py
          --ignore=tests/python/test_contextbench_ts.py
          --junitxml=pytest.xml
        env:
          PYTEST_ADDOPTS: -n auto --dist loadfile
      - name: Build the wheel and sdist
        run: uv build --out-dir dist
      # A lock can hide what a user's pip picks from the wheel's own metadata:
      # by default pip takes the newest release even when it has only an sdist.
      - name: Install the wheel with pip from its own metadata
        run: |
          venv="$RUNNER_TEMP/pip-wheel"
          uv venv -q --seed "$venv"
          python="$venv/bin/python"; [ -x "$python" ] || python="$venv/Scripts/python.exe"
          wheel=$(ls dist/*.whl)
          "$python" -m pip install -q --dry-run --ignore-installed --report "$RUNNER_TEMP/pip.json" "$wheel"
          "$python" -I -c "
          import json, sys
          report = json.load(open(sys.argv[1], encoding='utf-8'))['install']
          built = [f\"{i['metadata']['name']} {i['metadata']['version']}\" for i in report
                   if not i['download_info']['url'].endswith('.whl')]
          sys.exit(f'pip would build from source: {built}' if built else 0)" "$RUNNER_TEMP/pip.json"
          "$python" -m pip install -q --only-binary :all: "$wheel"
          "$python" -m pip check
          (cd "$RUNNER_TEMP" && "$python" -I "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/scripts/smoke_dist.py" "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/fixtures")
      - name: Smoke-test each artifact in a fresh environment
        run: |
          uv export --locked --no-dev --no-emit-project --no-hashes -q -o "$RUNNER_TEMP/requirements.txt"
          for artifact in dist/*.whl dist/*.tar.gz; do
            venv="$RUNNER_TEMP/smoke-$(basename "$artifact")"
            uv venv -q "$venv"
            # Third-party dependencies must ship wheels; only OXIDE's sdist is built.
            uv pip install -q --python "$venv" --only-binary :all: -r "$RUNNER_TEMP/requirements.txt"
            uv pip install -q --python "$venv" --no-deps "$artifact"
            uv pip check --python "$venv"
            python="$venv/bin/python"; [ -x "$python" ] || python="$venv/Scripts/python.exe"
            echo "== $artifact"
            (cd "$RUNNER_TEMP" && "$python" -I "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/scripts/smoke_dist.py" "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/fixtures")
          done
      - name: Keep the platform record
        # act (local runs) cannot copy this action into podman containers.
        if: always() && !env.ACT
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v5
        with:
          name: platform-${{ matrix.label }}
          path: |
            environment.json
            pytest.xml
            dist/
          if-no-files-found: ignore
name: CI

# OXIDE v2: runs exactly `mise run verify` — the same command used locally
# (Ruff, mypy --strict, pytest over the Python engine; ADR-0011).
on:
  pull_request:
    branches: [main, rewrite/v2]
  push:
    branches: [main]

# One run per change: PR runs cancel when superseded; main pushes (run_id) never do.
concurrency:
  group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.head_ref || github.run_id }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  verify:
    name: Verify
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
      - name: Install pinned uv
        uses: jdx/mise-action@v5
        with:
          version: 2026.9.14
          install_args: uv
      - name: Restore the ContextBench corpora cache
        uses: actions/cache@v6
        with:
          path: ~/.cache/oxide
          key: oxide-cache-linux-x86_64-${{ hashFiles('src/oxide/storage/ladybug.py', 'fixtures/eval/contextbench-py/tasks.json') }}
      # The corpora stay cached; the FTS build is always fetched cold, so a replaced
      # upstream build cannot hide behind the cache (docs/fts-mirror/RELEASE.md).
      - name: Drop the cached FTS extension
        run: rm -f ~/.cache/oxide/ladybug-extensions-*/libfts.lbug_extension
      - name: Install locked environment, verify the FTS extension, fetch the corpora
        run: mise run bootstrap
      - name: mise run verify
        run: mise run verify
        env:
          MISE_AUTO_INSTALL: "false"
          # Parallel in CI only; loadfile keeps a file's shared corpora fixture in one worker.
          PYTEST_ADDOPTS: -n auto --dist loadfile

"""Test isolation: every test gets a private data location; real user data is never touched.

The pinned FTS extension is a read-only dependency resolved from the real environment
(``OXIDE_FTS_EXTENSION`` or the default cache) before anything is redirected.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import os
import shutil
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile
from collections.abc import Iterator, Mapping
from pathlib import Path

import pytest

from oxide.storage.fts import _fts_build, fts_location, fts_unavailable
from oxide.storage.ladybug import default_data_dir

REPO = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]
FIXTURE = REPO / "fixtures" / "py_repo"
FTS = fts_location()
REAL_DATA = default_data_dir()


def _state(path: Path) -> object:
    return (
        sorted((str(p), p.stat().st_mtime_ns) for p in path.rglob("*")) if path.exists() else None
    )


@pytest.fixture(scope="session", autouse=True)
def real_data_untouched() -> Iterator[None]:
    before = _state(REAL_DATA)
    yield
    assert _state(REAL_DATA) == before, f"tests modified real user data at {REAL_DATA}"


@pytest.fixture(autouse=True)
def private_data(tmp_path: Path, monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch) -> Path:
    data = tmp_path / "oxide-data"
    monkeypatch.setenv("OXIDE_FTS_EXTENSION", str(FTS))
    monkeypatch.setenv("OXIDE_DATA_DIR", str(data))
    monkeypatch.setenv("XDG_DATA_HOME", str(tmp_path / "xdg-data"))
    monkeypatch.setenv("XDG_CACHE_HOME", str(tmp_path / "xdg-cache"))
    monkeypatch.delenv("TYPESAFE_API_KEY", raising=False)  # a real key never reaches a test
    for name in [k for k in os.environ if k.lower().endswith("_proxy")]:
        monkeypatch.delenv(name)  # localhost judges are reached directly
    return data


@pytest.fixture
def fts() -> Path:
    if _fts_build() is None:
        pytest.skip("no pinned FTS build for this platform (docs/platforms.md)")
    reason = fts_unavailable(FTS)
    assert reason is None, f"{reason} (lexical tests need the pinned extension)"

# Crash injection: the child dies (os._exit, no cleanup) at one publication step.
CRASH = textwrap.dedent(
    """
    import os, sys, oxide
    import oxide.storage.store as storage
    root, data, step = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2], sys.argv[3]
    real_rename, real_write, real_fsync = os.rename, storage._write_atomic, storage._fsync
    def fsync(path):
        if step == "in-seal" and path.name == "source":  # blobs linked, not yet published
            os._exit(9)
        real_fsync(path)
    def rename(src, dst):
        if step == "between-renames" and str(src).endswith(".staging"):
            os._exit(9)
        real_rename(src, dst)
    def write_atomic(path, data):
        if step == "before-current" and path.name == "CURRENT":
            os._exit(9)
        real_write(path, data)
        if step == "after-current" and path.name == "CURRENT":
            os._exit(9)
    storage.os.rename = rename
    storage._write_atomic = write_atomic
    storage._fsync = fsync
    with oxide.open_repository(root, data_dir=data) as repo:
        repo.index()
    sys.exit(3)
    """
)


def crash(repo: Path, data: Path, step: str) -> None:
    result = python(data, CRASH, str(repo), str(data), step)
    assert result.returncode == 9, result.stderr


def test_a_crash_between_the_rebuild_renames_is_undone_on_open(
    repo_copy: Path, private_data: Path, fts: Path
) -> None:
    first = oxide.index_repository(repo_copy)
    blobs(private_data)[0].unlink()  # same snapshot, unreadable: rebuilt under its name
    crash(repo_copy, private_data, "between-renames")
    name = (store_dir(private_data) / "CURRENT").read_text()
    generations = store_dir(private_data) / "generations"
    assert not (generations / name).exists() and (generations / f"{name}.replaced").is_dir()
    with oxide.open_repository(repo_copy) as repo:
        assert sorted(p.name for p in generations.iterdir()) == [name]
        report = repo.index()

def cache_dir() -> Path:

"""Test isolation: every test gets a private data location; real user data is never touched.

The pinned FTS extension is a read-only dependency resolved from the real environment
(``OXIDE_FTS_EXTENSION`` or the default cache) before anything is redirected.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import os
import shutil
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile
from collections.abc import Iterator, Mapping
from pathlib import Path

import pytest

from oxide.storage.fts import _fts_build, fts_location, fts_unavailable
from oxide.storage.ladybug import default_data_dir

REPO = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]
FIXTURE = REPO / "fixtures" / "py_repo"
FTS = fts_location()
REAL_DATA = default_data_dir()


def _state(path: Path) -> object:
    return (
        sorted((str(p), p.stat().st_mtime_ns) for p in path.rglob("*")) if path.exists() else None
    )


@pytest.fixture(scope="session", autouse=True)
def real_data_untouched() -> Iterator[None]:
    before = _state(REAL_DATA)
    yield
    assert _state(REAL_DATA) == before, f"tests modified real user data at {REAL_DATA}"


@pytest.fixture(autouse=True)
def private_data(tmp_path: Path, monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch) -> Path:
    data = tmp_path / "oxide-data"
    monkeypatch.setenv("OXIDE_FTS_EXTENSION", str(FTS))
    monkeypatch.setenv("OXIDE_DATA_DIR", str(data))
    monkeypatch.setenv("XDG_DATA_HOME", str(tmp_path / "xdg-data"))
    monkeypatch.setenv("XDG_CACHE_HOME", str(tmp_path / "xdg-cache"))
    monkeypatch.delenv("TYPESAFE_API_KEY", raising=False)  # a real key never reaches a test
    for name in [k for k in os.environ if k.lower().endswith("_proxy")]:
        monkeypatch.delenv(name)  # localhost judges are reached directly
    return data


@pytest.fixture
def fts() -> Path:
    if _fts_build() is None:
        pytest.skip("no pinned FTS build for this platform (docs/platforms.md)")
    reason = fts_unavailable(FTS)
    assert reason is None, f"{reason} (lexical tests need the pinned extension)"
    return FTS


@pytest.fixture
def repo_copy(tmp_path: Path) -> Path:
    """A private, writable copy of the Python fixture repository."""
    target = tmp_path / "py_repo"
    shutil.copytree(FIXTURE, target)
    return target


def write(root: Path, files: Mapping[str, str | bytes]) -> Path:
    for name, content in files.items():
        path = root / name
        path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        # Exact bytes: write_text would turn "\n" into "\r\n" on Windows.
        path.write_bytes(content if isinstance(content, bytes) else content.encode())
    return root


def env(data: Path) -> dict[str, str]:
    """Environment for a subprocess: explicit private data and cache locations.
    Fails closed unless ``data`` is test-owned (under the temporary root)."""
    if not data.resolve().is_relative_to(Path(tempfile.gettempdir()).resolve()):
        raise RuntimeError(f"{data} is not a private test location")
    return {
        **os.environ,
        "OXIDE_DATA_DIR": str(data),
        "OXIDE_FTS_EXTENSION": str(FTS),
        "XDG_DATA_HOME": str(data / "xdg"),
        "XDG_CACHE_HOME": str(data / "cache"),
    }


def python(data: Path, script: str, *args: str) -> subprocess.CompletedProcess[str]:
    """Runs ``script`` in a fresh interpreter with private locations: native probes that
    could crash, and crash injection, never run in the test process."""
    command = [sys.executable, "-c", script, *args]
    return subprocess.run(command, env=env(data), capture_output=True, text=True, check=False)

content.text:
I've made three CI changes. `mise run verify` passes locally (438 passed, 7 skipped, 2m43s), but I haven't measured the CI speed-up yet. That needs a pushed branch, and the rules here don't let me push without your OK.

**What the runs showed** (Platforms run 41298189655 and others)
- **Windows pytest is the slowest step** at about 395s, against 45–53s on Linux. Most of the gap is fsync calls in the storage layer: each costs about 85ms on the Windows runner, and the suite makes about 7,100 of them. That correlates at 0.80 with the extra Windows time per test. Defender is already off on `windows-2025`, so it isn't the cause.
- **Installing dependencies is not a bottleneck.** `uv sync` takes 2–22s, so adding a uv cache isn't worth it.
- **The ContextBench corpora cache kept missing.** Its key included `src/oxide/storage/ladybug.py`, which changed four times in PR #45, so each change forced a cold 96s bootstrap.
- **Changing how pytest-xdist splits tests across workers wouldn't help.** A simulated ideal split comes out the same (318s vs 317s).
- **Linux x86_64 was checked twice per run:** ci.yml's Verify job and Platforms' `linux-x86_64` row both ran mypy and pytest.

**Changes (uncommitted)**
1. **`tests/python/conftest.py`:** a new `no_fsync` fixture applies to every test and turns off `_fsync` inside the test process. No test can observe durability anyway. Tests that start subprocesses (crash injection, CLI, `smoke_dist.py`) still flush for real, so recovery coverage stays. Expected result: Windows pytest drops from about 395s to well under half (estimated, not measured), and macOS Intel also gets faster.
2. **`.github/workflows/ci.yml`:**
   - The cache now holds only `~/.cache/oxide/contextbench`, keyed on `tasks.json`.
   - I removed the step that deleted the FTS build, because the FTS build is no longer in the cache. It is still fetched cold on every run, so that release gate is unchanged.
   - I pinned the runner to `ubuntu-24.04`, the image `docs/platforms.md` lists as supported. Trade-off: CI no longer tests on `ubuntu-latest` (currently 26.04).
3. **`.github/workflows/platforms.yml`:** the `linux-x86_64` row now skips mypy and pytest, because Verify runs them on the same image. That row still builds and smokes the wheel, and the py3.12 and py3.14 rows still run the full suite.

I left Intel macOS alone: it already doesn't run on PRs, and its 130s mypy happened in only one run.

**Next step:** if you approve, I'll push a branch (not `main`) and compare its step times with the numbers above.

Not checked: the actual speed-up on CI. Product risk you should know about: Windows users pay about 85ms per file when indexing from scratch, because of the per-file fsync. I haven't fixed that here.

questions.question: I need real CI timings for the OXIDE changes: Windows/macOS pytest with fsync turned off in tests, the narrower ContextBench cache, and skipping the duplicated Linux tests. Can I commit them to a new branch `ci/speedup` and push it? On push, both CI and Platforms run. Intel macOS runs only on main pushes, so it needs a manual workflow_dispatch run if that trigger exists. Neither main nor rewrite/v2 is touched.

options.label: Push branch (Recommended)
options.description: Commit to ci/speedup, push it, start the runs and compare step times with the earlier baseline. I won't open a PR.

options.label: Push and open draft PR
options.description: Same, plus a draft PR to main so the PR-triggered workflows and their timings run too.

options.label: Don't push
options.description: Leave the changes uncommitted. The speed-up stays an estimate.

content.content:
name: Platforms

# Cross-platform verification of the Python engine (docs/platforms.md): on every
# supported platform, the locked environment installs, `oxide prepare` fetches that
# platform's pinned FTS build, mypy and the test suite run from the checkout, and the
# built wheel and sdist pass scripts/smoke_dist.py from a fresh environment.
# ContextBench quality gates stay in ci.yml (Linux) and `mise run contextbench-ts`.
on:
  pull_request:
    branches: [main, rewrite/v2]
  push:
    branches: [main]
  workflow_dispatch:

# One run per change: PR runs cancel when superseded; main pushes (run_id) never do.
concurrency:
  group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.head_ref || github.run_id }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

permissions:
name: CI

# OXIDE v2: runs exactly `mise run verify` — the same command used locally
# (Ruff, mypy --strict, pytest over the Python engine; ADR-0011).
on:
  pull_request:
    branches: [main, rewrite/v2]
  push:
    branches: [main]

# One run per change: PR runs cancel when superseded; main pushes (run_id) never do.
concurrency:
  group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.head_ref || github.run_id }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

permissions:
  contents: read

lines: -# Handoff 2026-10-04: #43 frozen run + TreeIndex/TreeRouter implementation
-Two independent work streams. Read `AGENTS.md` (= `CLAUDE.md`) and the memory notes
-(`local-model-limits`, `tree-direction`) first.
-## Stream 1 — #43 cap-removal validation (running unattended; finish and report)
-- **What:** arm B (the shipped selector without the 5-primary and 2-per-file caps, token-matched to
-  A) vs A on fresh tasks. The protocol is frozen at `b400c13` (`docs/cap-removal-eval/PROTOCOL.md` =
-  the #43 issue body). History and disclosures: `docs/cap-removal-eval/README.md` (two pauses, the
-  clap/zod worktree cleanups, the phase split, the pilot result: 30 tasks, B vs A +0.068, 3/0,
-  descriptive only).
-- **Running now:** detached chain `bash …/scratchpad/phase23.sh`, PID **235332**
-  `/tmp/claude-1000/-home-khoi-Projects-oxide/6037cda2-95b0-4329-9466-d9899710274a/scratchpad/phase23.log`.
-  A copy of the script is in `docs/cap-removal-eval/phases/phase23.sh`. Sequence:
-  1. `docs/cap-removal-eval/scripts/gen_all.sh b400c13`: held-out raw (7/8 repos done at handoff;
-     axios next), parent indexes and filters, `build_tasks.py heldout`, then the ContextBench draw
-     (seed 43). This is hours of capped indexing.
-  2. `run.py parity`, `run.py arms`, `run.py rss`, then `score.py`.
-  3. The verdict lands in `docs/cap-removal-eval/results/result.txt` (+ `result.json`,
-     `per_task.tsv`, `packs.jsonl`, `parity_p1.tsv`, `rss_o1.tsv`), in the **main** checkout.
-- **If the chain dies:** every stage is idempotent. Rerun `bash docs/cap-removal-eval/scripts/gen_all.sh b400c13`,
-  then `~/.cache/oxide-typed-eval/venv/bin/python docs/cap-removal-eval/scripts/run.py {parity,arms,rss}`
-  and `…/score.py`. That venv has numpy and pyarrow; the system python3 has neither.
-  - If a held-out repo stage was interrupted (raw file without `.done`), first remove that repo's
-    partial worktrees under `~/.cache/oxide-capremoval-eval/wt/<repo>-*` with
-    `git -C ~/.cache/oxide-jev-eval/repos/<repo> worktree remove --force …`. `make_tasks.py` reuses
-    an existing worktree without re-indexing it. Disclose any interruption in the README.
-- **When done, with no extra experiments:**
-  1. Write the verdict and the R1 regression causes into `docs/cap-removal-eval/README.md`.
-  2. Commit `docs/cap-removal-eval/results/`.
-  3. Post the outcome as a comment on #43, preserving a negative result if it is one.
-- **Disposition rules** (from the protocol): validity needs ≥ 50 held-out, ≥ 50 ContextBench and
-  ≥ 6 held-out repos, and P1 must pass; otherwise INCONCLUSIVE. Q1, Q2 or E1 failing → REJECT. All
-  gates passing → PASS. Q1, Q2 and E1 passing but R1 or O1 failing → NOT PASSED.
-## Stream 2 — TreeIndex / TreeRouter (inline plan execution, Task 1 in progress)
-- **Spec:** `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-04-treeindex-treerouter-design.md` (approved).
-  **Plan:** `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-10-04-treeindex-treerouter.md` (approved; the user chose
-  **Native** = inline execution with the `superpowers:executing-plans` skill, plus one fresh
-  whole-branch review at the end).
-- **Worktree:** `/home/khoi/Projects/oxide-treeindex`, branch `feat/treeindex` (base `e03fd2b`).
-  Never implement on `main`.
-- **Ledger:** `/home/khoi/Projects/oxide-treeindex/.superpowers/sdd/2026-10-04-treeindex-treerouter/progress.md`
-  (pre-flight rows and one ruling). Task scripts:
-  `~/.claude/plugins/cache/anthropic-plugin-directory/superpowers/6.4.2-8ca22dba9a94/skills/executing-plans/scripts/{task-start,task-done}`.
-- **Task 1 state:** RED, verified.
-  - `tests/tree_storage.rs` is new (3 tests) and `tests/index_generation.rs` gained 4 tree steps.
-    Both are **uncommitted**.
-  - They fail to compile on the missing `oxide::tree`, `write_tree_files`, `put_tree_vectors`,
-    `clear_tree_vectors` and `write_tree_dirs`.
-  - Next, implement per the plan:
-    - `src/tree/mod.rs` (constants, `NodeKind`, `TreeNode`, `node_id` via `fnv1a64_iter`);
-    - the tree tables appended to `SCHEMA_SQL` in `src/storage/schema.rs`;
-    - `IndexRead` tree readers with empty default impls (`CountingStore` in `engine.rs` tests also
-      implements `IndexRead`);
-    - the `IndexWrite` tree writers in `src/storage/sqlite.rs`, each one IMMEDIATE transaction +
-      `bump_generation`.
-  - Implementation notes decided so far:
-    - use an UPSERT (`ON CONFLICT(id) DO UPDATE`), **not** `INSERT OR REPLACE`, for file nodes, so a
-      rewrite keeps the node's vector (test `rewriting_a_file_node_keeps_its_vector`);
-    - `tree_postings` is `WITHOUT ROWID`, PK `(term, node_id)`, plus an index on `node_id` for the
-      cascade (mirrors `lexical_postings`);
-    - file postings are SQL aggregates of `lexical_postings`/`lexical_docs` joined via `symbols.file`.

-- **Build/test:** `CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/home/khoi/Projects/oxide-treeindex/target systemd-run --user --scope -q -p MemoryMax=6G -p CPUQuota=200% nice -n 10 cargo test -j 2 --test tree_storage --test index_generation`.
-- **Gates in the plan:**
-  - Task 5 (Phase 0 dev): stop if no router beats flat recall@5.
-  - Task 6 (fresh validation, seed 44, **not** #43's tasks): stop on FAIL.
-  - Task 8 only preregisters Phase 1.
-  - Tasks 5–6 run embedding models: never concurrently with #43's chain (one model process at a
-    time). Wait for it to finish, or SIGSTOP its process group (`kill -STOP -- -235332`, later
-    `-CONT`) and disclose.
-## Gotchas learned this session
-- The GateGuard hook asks for "facts" before the first Bash command and before each new file's first
-  write or edit. Answer them briefly, then retry.
-- `pkill -f <pattern>` / `pgrep -f` match your **own** shell's command line (exit 144 kills your
-  shell). Kill by PID. Waiters whose command line contains a pattern block `pgrep`-based waits.
-- `setsid nohup cmd &` forks: the real PID is `$!`+1.
-- Git has no global identity. Commit with
-  `git -c user.name="Khoi Truong" -c user.email="tannguyenkhoitruong@gmail.com" commit …` and end the
-  message with the `Claude-Session:` trailer line.
-- Local commits go to `main` (`docs/agents/workflow.md`). **Nothing has been pushed**, so don't push
-  unless asked.
-- Don't start shortlist-reranking experiments (#42 is closed; see memory `tree-direction`).
-## Lead (from #42; not yet validated)

-Tracked by #9. In #42, arm **B** (the shipped flat selector *without* the 5-primary and 2-per-file caps, packed to exactly the shipped pack's `used_tokens`) beat the shipped selector **A** on the 149 frozen #40 tasks:
-| | Δ gold-line coverage (repo-clustered 95 % CI) | rel/used | up/down |
-Source: `docs/treeselect-eval/results/` (`per_task.tsv`, `result.txt`, the `B vs A` comparison).
-**Why it is a lead, not a result**
-- It was a reported, non-gated comparison, and it is in-sample for this task set.
-- It is held-out-driven: ContextBench's coverage CI includes 0.

-- It differs from the allocator studies' rejected top-ups (ch1, ch5, ch7). It **reallocates slots at the same tokens** instead of adding tokens. ch5 failed E1 because it spent extra tokens; here efficiency rises.
-**What it would take** (not started; needs its own preregistration):

-- Freeze B's exact rule. It is the role-then-score order with the 1-test cap, dedup, floor and shrink-to-fit unchanged. Because the caps no longer bound the pack, a budget or stop rule has to be decided: either keep the shipped 4096 budget with a stop rule, or define a token target.
-- Evaluate once on **fresh** tasks that played no part in #42, with ch5-style gates (coverage CI > 0, efficiency lower bound ≥ −5 %, per-stratum non-negative, latency/RSS, byte parity).
-- Keep this separate from TreeSelect v1, which is being diagnosed on the #42 tasks as a development set.
-Production is unchanged.
-## Preregistered validation (added 2026-10-04, before any fresh task exists)
-TreeSelect is stopped: the #42 v1 diagnosis (`docs/treeselect-eval/v1-dev/`) found no hierarchy lever at this seam. This issue validates the one effect with a development signal.

-**Research only. Production unchanged.** Retrieval, RRF (K=60, 0.6/0.4, depth 200), embeddings, `symbol_embed_text`, the schema, ids and the CLI/MCP/JSON output stay frozen. The arms run through #42's committed, never-merged `docs/treeselect-eval/research.patch`, applied unmodified (arm B's code path did not change in amendment 1).
-### Question
-**At equal tokens, does removing the 5-primary and 2-per-file caps from the shipped selector improve final-context quality on fresh tasks?**
-### Arms (frozen; exactly #42's definitions)
-| arm | rule |
-| **A** | the shipped selector (16 seeds, budget 4096) |

-| **B** | the shipped pipeline (same seeds, production expansion and evidence, dedup, floor, role-then-score order, 350-token windows with shrink-to-fit, 1-test cap) **without the 5-primary and 2-per-file caps**, with the budget set per task to A's `used_tokens` |
-Harness: `examples/treeselect_pack.rs --arms A,B` from that patch, using the archived #42 amended binary.
-### Fresh data

-- **Held-out.** The same 8 upstream clones as #40/#42. `make_tasks.py` runs unmodified with `max_tasks=20` per repo, in its git-log order. Exclusions come from #40's `excl.py`, unmodified, run at this protocol's frozen commit: every SHA, parent and instance in any committed `docs/**/*.jsonl[.gz]` / `eval-agent/**/*.jsonl` file, which includes all of #40's and #42's tasks and draws. Then, as #40: parent corpora, ch5's parent gold filter and near-duplicate rule, edit-locus gold, fallback exclusion, #40's eligibility rule, and the **first 10 eligible tasks per repo**.

-- **ContextBench.** The pinned parquet (`2f56535b…`), excluding every instance id in that committed text. #40's per-stratum round-robin draw runs unmodified with **seed 43** and the same targets (description 25, quoted 34, other 10), the same checkout, index and eligibility rule, and line gold from `gold_context`.

-- **Population.** #40's eligibility rule is kept so that the fresh population matches the development population. It keeps tasks whose gold files appear in, but do not fill, the fused top-50 file view.
-- **Repo identity.** A repo is the lowercased upstream `owner/name`, and the same upstream in both sets is one repo. Repos may overlap the development set; tasks may not.
-- **Generation scripts** (`docs/cap-removal-eval/scripts/`) are committed with this protocol before generation. They change only paths, the seed and the exclusion source.
-### Metrics, CIs and gates

-- Metrics are #42's: `score_alloc.pack_metrics` with each task's line gold. CIs use #42's repo-clustered paired bootstrap (repos with replacement, then tasks within each drawn repo; 10,000 resamples; a fresh `numpy.random.default_rng(0)` per analysis; repos sorted).
-- E1's relative efficiency is ch5's definition, computed within each resample. Tasks where A used 0 tokens are dropped from efficiency.
-- A task-level bootstrap (10,000, seed 0) is reported as descriptive only.
-| gate | rule (B vs A) |
-| Q1 | pooled gold-line coverage Δ: 95 % CI lower bound > 0 |
-| Q2 | neither stratum (held-out, ContextBench) has a negative point Δ |
-| E1 | pooled rel/used relative Δ: CI lower bound ≥ −5 % |
